topic: Texas option period: why 10 days is really 6
hook: Buyers pay for 10 option days. Most only get 6.

scores.worst_problem: The hook states the arithmetic conclusion outright (10 becomes 6), so a savvy buyer can half-guess the payoff — scheduling and report lag — before swiping.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 1 to withhold the number, e.g. "You paid for 10 option days. Your inspector already took most of them." — keep the loss vivid but the size and cause unstated.

topic: Texas transplant reality check: pick the city before the house
hook: The house is the last thing you should pick.

scores.worst_problem: The hook states a familiar real-estate truism ('location before house'), so a reader can half-guess the payoff without swiping.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 1 to withhold a Texas-specific consequence instead of the generic principle — e.g. 'Four filters run before the house. Skip the third and it costs you every month.'

topic: Texas market reality check: hidden discounts and the two speed market
hook: Texas has 7 months of inventory. That number is lying.

scores.worst_problem: Slide 3's loop, "Your speed is set early," is abstract restatement of the two-speeds point rather than a withheld promise, so it pulls weakest of the five.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 3's loop into a concrete withheld consequence tied to the next slide, e.g. "You get fourteen days, total."
